newsitem.title: USA: Vermont unemployment slips to 3.9 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Vermont unemployment slips to 3.9 pct in January.

text.p: Vermont's unemployment rate fell 0.7 to 3.9 percent in January, buoyed by rises in trade and services, but the state warned that the job gains might have been a bit exaggerated.

"Unemployment appeared to improve in January, but the drop may be slightly overstated," said Susan Auld, commissioner of the state Department of Employment and Training, in prepared remarks. In December, the unemployment rate stood at 4.6 percent, and the latest report also showed a stronger economy than a year-ago, when the level was 4.5 percent.

Employment rose by 1,300, with roughly the same number of jobs added by services and retail trade, as the usual drop after the holiday season might have been moderated by the opening of some new enterprises, the state said.

The only industry that had a net job increase in January was services, mainly due to winter recreation activities, according to unseasonally adjusted data. Manufacturing employment fell significantly, though stone-cutting and construction turned down less than usual.

Overall, nonfarm jobs rose by 1.7 percent from a Overall, nonfarm jobs rose by 1.7 percent from a year-ago. In Vermont's 13 labor markets, the unemployment rate ranged from 2.3 percent in Hartford-Lebanon to 11.2 percent in Newport, according to unseasonally adjusted data. When measured on this basis for the entire state, the rate was five percent.
